title: Arlington Boulevard 16-unit stacked townhouse proposal
subtitle: Reduced parking, drainage, bike storage and amenity space discussed for a three-storey rental building near Weber Street.
overview: The Planning and Strategic Initiatives Committee held a short meeting with one item: applications to redevelop 44 and 50 Arlington Boulevard, at the corner of Weber Street East. The committee recommended approving an Official Plan amendment and a zoning by-law amendment {{vote:m1}}.

The change would let two detached homes be replaced with a three-storey, 16-unit stacked townhouse building of rental units. The plan includes eight surface parking spaces and 16 bicycle spaces. The land use stays low-rise residential, but the amendments allow more floor space, reduced parking and a smaller side yard setback. A holding provision requires final approval of a noise study before development proceeds.

For residents, this adds rental housing on a high-frequency transit route in an established neighbourhood. Neighbours had raised traffic, parking, drainage, garbage bin location and fencing concerns. As a standing committee, this group only makes a recommendation. Council must still ratify it, and detailed design will be settled later at site plan approval.

decisions.item: Official Plan amendment, 44 and 50 Arlington Boulevard
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the Official Plan amendment, which adds a site-specific policy allowing a higher floor space ratio for the property.

decisions.item: Zoning by-law amendment, 44 and 50 Arlington Boulevard
decisions.detail: The committee recommended rezoning the site to allow a 16-unit multiple dwelling, with reduced parking, more floor space, a smaller side yard setback and a holding provision tied to a noise study.

debate: Staff and the applicant's consultants described the project as compatible "missing middle" housing on a corner lot, near a high-frequency bus route, groceries and a drugstore.

Parking was a resident concern. The applicant's consultants said a parking study supported about one space for every two units, and that rentals would not be tied to specific spaces. One councillor suggested going lower on parking and adding more amenity space, since residents would have no backyard.

The applicant said detailed parking and amenity questions can be refined at site plan stage. The chair noted the site-specific zoning sets amenity space requirements, so reductions would require going to the Committee of Adjustment.

On drainage, raised by a neighbouring resident, the applicant's team said City and Regional engineering staff reviewed the servicing and stormwater report. They said underground storage chambers with infiltration would keep water on the property, since there is no storm sewer on that part of Arlington.

Councillors also asked about bicycle storage, which would be outside on the east side with some secure lockers and some open spaces. They asked about the small seating area and balconies, and confirmed the site is outside the Growing Together study area.
